newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA FOREIGN MINISTRY PINS HOPES ON HELSINKI.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA FOREIGN MINISTRY PINS HOPES ON HELSINKI.

text.p: Romania expects this week's U.S.-Russian summit in Helsinki to validate Central European countries' bid to join the Atlantic Alliance, foreign ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said on Wednesday.
Lazar said the United States' official position showed clearly that "a second Yalta" -- a reference to Europe's post-war division into spheres of influence -- "is now inconceivable."

"The context of international relations today is totally different and such a possibility (a second Yalta) would mean the two (U.S. and Russian) leaders would want to revert to a past which was not a quite happy one," she said.
The ministry's weekly news briefing also included:
* Foreign Minister Adrian Severin will meet his Portuguese counterpart during a visit to Lisbon starting March 26 and brief the Portuguese leaders on Romania's efforts to join NATO in the first wave.
* EU finance and economy ministers have unlocked a 70 million ECU tranche to support Romania's balance of payments from a credit granted by the Group of the 24 industrialised countries in 1994.
* Junior foreign ministry officials will discuss the stage of Romanian-Russian relations in Moscow on March 28.
* Exiled King Michael, who was recently issued with a Romanian diplomatic passport, will start his mission to support the country's bid to join NATO in the first wave, next week in London.
